list: The official 55 trophies, as PlayStation publishes them (names, descriptions and grades checked against Exophase and PSNProfiles on 19 Nov 2026; the two agree on every name, description and grade)
note: Every guide below is written in our own words for this guide. Specific places and steps are only claimed where the official description or a cited source pins them down; the game released on 19 Nov 2026 and no in-game route has been verified yet, so anything beyond the official description is labelled as advice from the description, not a verified fact.

exophase.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI Trophies (official list)

own.name: Our own advice, from the official description — not yet verified in-game

psnprofiles.name: PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI Trophies (PSN counts)

trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is nothing extra to do for it. Work the roadmap in order (story first, then strangers, then collectibles and activities, then the partner-crime cleanup) and this is the last trophy you will hear. PSN tracks it at 0.1% of players so far, which is expected on launch day.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to its end — it is the first mission of the game, so just follow the story from the start and this pops before anything else can be missed. It cannot be skipped: the mission is the game's opening, and PSN already shows most launch-day players earning it. If you are past the opening and do not have it, replay the mission from the story menu if the game offers replays.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1, in order — the trophy is awarded when the chapter's final mission ends. Play the story straight through without detouring into long side grinds, and keep a manual save before the chapter's last mission so a missed story beat can be retried. The exact mission list inside the chapter is not published in the official description, so no mission names are claimed here.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 2 — the trophy pops when the chapter closes. The chapter trophy is story-gated, so it cannot be earned early or out of order; if you rush the main path, you will reach it naturally. Keep a save from before the chapter's final mission, in case any mission inside it holds a one-time choice.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 3 — the trophy is awarded at the chapter's end. By this point the map and side systems are open, but the chapter trophy only needs the main missions done; side content can wait for the cleanup stages. Save before the chapter's final mission, as with the earlier chapters.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 4 — the last numbered chapter trophy. Once it pops, the endgame and the final mission are ahead; this is the point to check the Missables page before pushing on, because several partner and choice trophies are tied to story moments around here. The official description names only the chapter, not its missions, so no mission list is claimed.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Complete the final story mission — the gold trophy for finishing the story. Do the missable partner trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy) and any one-time choices before this mission if you can, because the story may not let you return to those moments afterwards; whether missions can be replayed after the credits is not yet verified in-game. After it pops, the open world stays open for the cleanup stages.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. It is a named mission inside the story, so it unlocks as you play the chapters in order — keep playing the main path and it will appear. If a mission can be missed, it is this kind: a single named mission, so take it when it is offered and do not rush past its prompt.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heists in this series are usually multi-part, so expect setup missions before the heist itself counts — the trophy is for the heist mission, so follow the story prompts until it is offered and finish it. The official description names only the mission, so no setup list is claimed here.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Like the other named-mission trophies, it arrives by playing the chapters in order — the mission is offered by the story, not found in the open world. Do it when it appears; named missions are the ones most likely to be missable if you push the story past them without answering.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. Follow the main story until the mission is offered, then finish it — the trophy is tied to that one mission, so the only way to miss it is to pass the story point where it is offered. The official description gives the mission name only, so no location or setup detail is claimed here.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, at the airport (VCIA is Vice City International Airport, named in the mission itself). Play the story in order until the mission unlocks. The same mission name also appears in the Catch Me If You Can trophy, so the airport is a place to return to after the story for the open-world stunt.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The name suggests a large set-piece mission late in the story, so expect it in the final stretch of the chapters — keep playing the main path and it will be offered. As with every named mission, take it when it appears rather than leaving it for later.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion — PSN tracks this as a count to 100, and it is the game's second gold trophy for a reason: it needs the story, the stranger strands, the collectibles and the activities all done. Treat it as a checklist, not a grind: finish the roadmap's stages in order and watch the in-game completion percentage climb. The exact list of what counts toward 100% is not published in the official description, so this guide does not claim a fixed checklist for it — use the in-game stats page as the source of truth.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — PSN tracks the count to 250, so this is a long grind best done a little at a time while you travel. Any jump, near-miss or airtime the game counts as a stunt adds to the total, so take ramps and jumps whenever you are driving between missions instead of saving it all for the end. The official description does not say which moves count, so the exact stunt list is not claimed here — watch the PSN counter climb.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once — PSN tracks the count to 9. The activities are the game's side systems (shooting range, drone races, races, fishing, arcade games, bowling, hunting and the rest); sample one of each as they unlock rather than grinding one. If one type is still locked, it is probably tied to story progress, so come back after the next chapter.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — PSN tracks the count to 42. Work through the range's challenges one weapon or drill at a time, and replay any that only give silver or bronze until the gold threshold is met. Gold medals are a skill bar, not a location puzzle, so practice the drill that is failing you instead of hunting for a shortcut; no challenge list is claimed here because the official description does not publish one.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every one of the 14 locations — PSN tracks the count to 14. Visit each Top Fun location, enter its drone race and win it; the trophy needs a win at each place, not just a finish. Do these after the story opens the whole map, and keep a note of which locations are already won so you do not repeat one by mistake.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — PSN tracks the count to 20, and the word different matters: winning the same race twice only counts once. Enter a spread of races across the map (street, off-road and whatever else the game offers) and win each one once. Races are an activity, so they stay available after the story; the list of race events is not published in the official description, so no event list is claimed.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a named fishing rival, so find the fishing challenge where he appears and out-fish him — fishing challenges are an activity, and the challenge is against Cal specifically, not just any catch. PSN already shows this as one of the most-earned trophies on launch day, so the challenge is available early. The exact spot is not published in the official description, so no location is claimed here.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — any arcade game, once, from start to finish. Find an arcade machine in the world, play until the game ends (a win or a full playthrough, not just starting it), and the trophy pops. This is the easiest activity trophy, so do it early to tick off one of the 9 activity types for Master of None as well.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Andy's stranger strand. Stranger missions are side content offered by named characters around Leonida — meet Andy, work through every mission he offers, and the trophy pops at his last one. Do not leave a stranger's strand half-finished before the story ends: whether strands stay available after the final mission is not yet verified in-game, so finish each one when it is offered.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Kenton's stranger strand — meet Kenton, finish each mission he offers in turn, and the trophy pops at the last. Stranger strands are the side-mission chains counted toward Strangers & Freaks, so Kenton's strand also moves that silver trophy forward. Finish it before the final story mission, in case strands close off afterwards.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Billy's stranger strand. Work through Billy's missions as they appear around Leonida and the trophy pops at his last one. Billy is one of five named stranger contacts with a final-mission trophy (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone), so keep a note of whose strand is finished and whose is still open.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida — PSN tracks the count to 8. A strand is a whole chain of missions for one stranger, so finishing one person's chain counts once; the five named final-mission trophies (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are five of the eight. Find strangers by their markers around the state, finish each chain, and keep the count moving during the story rather than leaving all eight for the endgame.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Randy's stranger strand — meet Randy, play through his missions in order, and the trophy pops at the last. Like the other stranger finals, it is safest to finish Randy's chain while the story is still running, because whether strands remain open after the credits is not yet verified in-game.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Tyrone's stranger strand. Tyrone's chain is the fifth named stranger final, and finishing it also counts toward the 8 strands of Strangers & Freaks. Work his missions as they appear; if a mission only appears in a certain area or at a certain story point, answer it then rather than assuming it will wait.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida — PSN tracks the count to 18. Meditation spots are quiet places scattered around the state; visit each one and meditate there, and the trophy pops at the last. This is a collectible-style sweep best done after the story opens the full map, with a route that covers each region once; the spot list is not published in the official description, so no map of spots is claimed here.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret is a stranger contact tied to hunting, so his strand will point you at the animal — follow his missions until the hunt is offered, then take the animal down. The official description names the animal only as unique, so no species or location is claimed here; the hunt is the point, and it is Bret's missions that lead to it.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 Collectible Card sets — find and collect the cards scattered across Leonida until three full sets are done. Cards are a collectible sweep, so pick them up as you travel rather than leaving them for a final hunt; the official description gives no set list or card locations, so no map is claimed here.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations across Leonida — PSN tracks the count to 100. WAiNK is the in-game marking activity (the exact interaction is not yet verified in-game, so no button prompt or spot list is claimed here); work through locations as you explore the state and the count builds up. Best treated as a long sweep alongside the other collectibles.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 Challenges — PSN tracks the count to 50. Challenges are the game's assorted side objectives across races, stunts, the shooting range and other activities; clear them as you play and the total climbs. No fixed list of which 50 counts is published in the official description, so work the activities you enjoy and let the count build rather than hunting one specific challenge.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star Wanted Level, then lose the cops and escape. Easiest once you have a fast car and open road: raise the heat with your partner in the vehicle, then break line of sight and stay out of the search area until the stars clear. The trophy pops when the wanted level drops while your partner is with you.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob three shops in a row without losing your Wanted Level — the chain breaks if the heat drops between robberies, so keep the cops on you and move straight from one shop to the next. Plan a route of three nearby shops, keep a getaway vehicle close, and do not stop to lose the police until the third till is done.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles across Leonida — PSN tracks the count to 100. Driving, riding or otherwise encountering a new vehicle adds to the total, so sample everything you pass: cars, bikes, boats and aircraft all count toward discovery. This builds naturally as you explore; a dedicated sweep of vehicle-dense areas speeds it up.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during a single use of Combat Focus — the slow-motion aiming mode. Trigger Combat Focus in a fight with at least five enemies in range, and drop all five before the focus ends. Pick a mission or shootout with grouped enemies, and do not waste the window on cover or reloading; the trophy pops at the fifth takedown inside one activation.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — Vice City International Airport. The plain reading of the description is to take a plane and leave the airport without a schedule, i.e. get an aircraft airborne; the exact trigger is not yet verified in-game, so no runway or aircraft is claimed here. Head to the airport, get a plane airborne, and the trophy should pop on departure.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: Kinda hot in these Rhinos — the trophy is tied to the Rhino tank. The official description names no objective, so no specific feat is claimed here; the plain reading is to get behind the controls of a Rhino and use it. Once a Rhino is available to drive, take it out and put it through its paces until the trophy pops — the exact trigger is not yet verified in-game.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a clean stealth job. Case the store first, move quietly, take the goods and leave before any alarm or witness raises the heat. If you are spotted, the attempt fails, so back out and try again rather than fighting through; patience and a quiet approach are the whole trick.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 Bank Vaults and escape — PSN tracks the count to 5. Each vault job means getting inside, cracking the vault and getting out with the cops behind you, so bring a fast getaway and a planned route for every job. The count builds one vault at a time; five clean escapes and the trophy is yours.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an Armored Truck and escape. Armored trucks run set routes around the state — intercept one, stop it, crack it open and grab the cash, then lose the wanted level that follows. Bring heavy firepower to stop the truck and a fast car to get away; the trophy pops once you have escaped with the haul.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — visit every region of the state until the map is filled in. Drive, fly and sail through each area, including the outlying towns and countryside beyond Vice City itself; the trophy pops when the last unexplored corner is covered. Best done steadily during the story, with a final sweep of any blank patches on the map after the credits.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang — hit one illicit setup for every gang in Leonida. Illegal operations are gang-run spots around the state; find one per gang, rob it and get out. The official description gives no gang list or locations, so no count or map is claimed here — work through the gangs as their operations turn up.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — head to the beachfront in Ocean Beach, find a bar or spot with a view, and order a cocktail. A quiet moment trophy: no fight, no chase, just the drink and the view. The exact venue is not pinned down in the official description, so no specific bar is claimed here.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a car straight through a showroom's glass front and out the other side. Pick a showroom, line up a fast car, and floor it through the glass; the 'classic style' nod is to the old games, and the trophy pops once you have made your exit through the storefront.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley — go bowling. Head to the Kolt & Associates alley, play a game and follow through on your throws; the trophy is about showing up and playing rather than a high score. The exact trigger (a full game, a strike, or simply bowling) is not yet verified in-game, so no specific score is claimed here.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal — the official description gives no objective, so no specific feat is claimed here. The wording points at the Lucia-and-Jason partnership reaching a wide audience, most plausibly through the in-game social or fame side of their story; play the partnership content as it comes and the trophy should follow. Treat this as one to watch for as the story unfolds rather than one to hunt directly.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Choices made (for better or worse) — a story trophy for a decision point in the campaign. Somewhere in the story you will face a choice, and the trophy pops once you have made it, whichever way you go. Because a choice may lock out the other branch, make a manual save before the decision if you want to see both outcomes; the exact mission is not named in the official description, so no mission is claimed here.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Second time's the charm — the official description gives no objective, so no specific feat is claimed here. The plain reading is that something fails once and succeeds on the retry, so if an activity or event goes wrong the first time, try it again instead of moving on; the retry itself may be the trigger. Do not assume a failed first attempt is wasted — come back and do it again.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? — the official description gives no objective, so no specific feat is claimed here. The wording reads like a surprise or easter-egg moment, something strange you stumble into while exploring Leonida; keep an eye out for odd events and out-of-place encounters as you travel. This is one to earn by playing and noticing, not by following a checklist.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by — knock people down with a melee weapon while driving past. Get a melee weapon in hand, drive alongside a group on foot and swing as you pass; the trophy pops once the drive-by connects. Pick a busy sidewalk, keep your speed moderate so the swing lands, and mind the wanted level that follows.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts — PSN tracks the total to $250,000. Marked Bills come from robberies and other scores; pass them to your contacts to wash them into clean cash, and the total climbs with each laundered batch. Keep robbing, keep laundering, and the trophy pops at $250,000.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — PSN tracks the total to $100,000. Buy weapons, clothes, vehicles, food and anything else the shops of Leonida sell; every dollar counts toward the same pot. This builds naturally over a full playthrough, and late-game purchases make the last stretch easy.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties — buy every garage property available across Leonida. Garages are the properties that store your vehicle collection; save up, visit each one for sale and buy it. The official description gives no count or list, so no number is claimed here — work through the properties as they appear on the market.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — PSN tracks the count to 10. Use the Scooter Bros app to register vehicles you own or find, one at a time, until ten are on the books. Any ten vehicles count, so register the ones already in your garage first and top up with new finds.
trophies.name: On the Spot
